procedures.title: FCC Compliance Operation
preconditions: Device must be configured according to instructions
steps: Ensure device does not cause harmful interference
Accept any interference received, including interference causing undesired operation
Do not make unauthorized modifications to equipment
Input only properly assigned MMSI numbers
Input only accurate device data
procedures.expected_outcome: Device operates in compliance with FCC rules Part 15

procedures.title: Industry Canada Compliance Operation
preconditions: Device must be configured according to instructions
steps: Ensure device does not cause interference
Accept any interference received, including interference causing undesired operation

procedures.title: Initial Power Up
steps: Switch on power to the AIS transceiver
Verify indicator lights activate
Wait for initial system startup
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver powers up and enters operational mode

procedures.title: GPS Antenna Installation
preconditions: Mounting location selected with clear view of sky
steps: Select mounting location with clear view of sky
Mount GPS antenna using appropriate hardware
Route antenna cable to AIS transceiver
Connect to GPS antenna connector on unit
procedures.expected_outcome: GPS antenna securely mounted with clear signal reception

procedures.title: VHF Antenna Connection
steps: Locate VHF antenna connector on unit
Route VHF antenna cable to AIS transceiver
Connect antenna to VHF connector
procedures.expected_outcome: VHF antenna properly connected for AIS transmission/reception

procedures.title: External Switch Installation
steps: Locate external switch connection points
Route switch wiring to AIS transceiver
Connect switch wiring to appropriate terminals
procedures.expected_outcome: External switch properly connected and functional

procedures.title: NMEA 0183 Data Port Connection
steps: Identify NMEA 0183 connection points
Route data cables to AIS transceiver
Connect NMEA 0183 wiring to appropriate terminals
procedures.expected_outcome: NMEA 0183 data connection established

procedures.title: Safe Installation Distance Requirements
steps: Ensure antenna is mounted at least 1.5 meters away from the AIS transceiver
Mount antenna 3.5 meters above deck to meet RF exposure requirements
Maintain MPE radius of 0.6 meters from antenna
Ensure no one operates within MPE radius unless shielded by grounded metallic barrier
Do not co-locate antenna with other transmitting antennas
procedures.expected_outcome: Safe RF exposure levels maintained during operation

procedures.title: Antenna Requirements
steps: Verify antenna impedance is 50 ohms
Connect VHF antenna before applying power
Ensure antenna gain does not exceed 3 dB for standard MPE radius
procedures.expected_outcome: Proper antenna configuration for safe operation

procedures.title: Compass Safe Distance Maintenance
steps: Maintain minimum distance of 0.55 meters between unit and compass
Verify no compass deviation greater than 0.3° when properly distanced
procedures.expected_outcome: Accurate compass readings without interference

procedures.title: Product Disposal Procedure
steps: Dispose of AIS transceiver according to European WEEE Directive
Alternatively, follow local regulations for electrical equipment disposal
Separate packaging materials for recycling
Dispose of packaging through environmentally friendly means
procedures.expected_outcome: Proper disposal of equipment and packaging

procedures.title: Safety Installation Requirements
steps: Verify installation location is not in a flammable atmosphere
Ensure installation area is away from engine room
Maintain distance from fuel tanks
Follow all installation instructions in manual
procedures.expected_outcome: Safe installation environment established

procedures.title: AIS Static Data Configuration
preconditions: Must have valid VHF radiotelephone license
Must be performed by competent installer if in US waters
steps: Program Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI)
Enter vessel name
Enter vessel call sign (if available)
Configure vessel type
Input vessel dimensions
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver properly configured with static vessel data

procedures.title: US Configuration Requirements
preconditions: Must be used in US waters
Must be performed by authorized dealer/installer
steps: Contact dealer for proper configuration
Have competent installer enter MMSI
Have competent installer enter static data
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver properly configured for US waters operation

procedures.title: Dynamic Data Collection
preconditions: AIS antenna must be properly installed
steps: System automatically calculates location
System automatically calculates speed over ground (SOG)
System automatically calculates course over ground (COG)
procedures.expected_outcome: Real-time dynamic vessel data collected and transmitted

procedures.title: Package Contents Verification
steps: Verify presence of NAIS-500 unit
Verify Quick Start Guide
Verify Product manual
Verify Warranty information
Verify packet of 4 screws
Verify Power and data cable
Verify USB configuration cable
Check for optional items in kit 000-13609-001: T-Connector, GPS antenna, N2k cable
procedures.expected_outcome: All components present and accounted for

procedures.title: Support Tools CD Installation
steps: Insert CD into computer
Install NAIS System Configurator software
Install USB drivers
Access alternative language manuals if needed
procedures.expected_outcome: Required software and drivers installed successfully

procedures.title: AIS Transceiver Physical Installation
steps: Locate the four mounting holes on the AIS transceiver
Position unit in desired location
Install using provided fixing screws
Ensure GPS antenna has clear view of sky
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver securely mounted with proper GPS antenna positioning

procedures.title: Electrical Connections Setup
steps: Connect power supply
Connect NMEA 0183 data ports to chart-plotters
Connect USB port to PC/Mac if needed
Connect external switch for silent mode control
Connect NMEA 2000 port to compatible equipment
Install VHF antenna
Install external GPS antenna
procedures.expected_outcome: All electrical connections properly established

procedures.title: Installing NAIS-500 AIS Transceiver
preconditions: Have all necessary additional items from 'Preparing for installation' section
steps: Select location meeting following criteria:
Ensure 0.55m or greater compass safe distance for 0.3° deviation
Allow adequate cable routing space
Maintain ambient temperature between -15°C and +55°C
Avoid flammable/hazardous atmospheres
Mount vertically or horizontally
Install in 'below deck' environment
Use four supplied self-tapping screws to mount
Ensure indicators are visible
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver securely mounted in suitable location

procedures.title: Installing External GPS Antenna - Pole Mount
steps: Feed GPS antenna cable through pole
Mount pole into position
Fit GPS antenna to pole adapter using 2 small screws
procedures.expected_outcome: GPS antenna securely pole-mounted

procedures.title: Installing External GPS Antenna - Surface Mount
preconditions: Select flat clean surface with clear sky view
Ensure surface is clean without dirt/paint/debris
steps: Mark and drill 2 mounting holes and cable hole
Install gasket by threading cable through center
Screw GPS antenna to mounting surface
Route cable to AIS transceiver
Connect cable to GPS connector on transceiver
procedures.expected_outcome: GPS antenna securely surface-mounted and connected

procedures.title: Connecting VHF Antenna
steps: Route cable from VHF antenna to AIS transceiver
Connect to VHF connector on AIS transceiver
procedures.expected_outcome: VHF antenna successfully connected to transceiver

procedures.title: VHF Antenna Installation
steps: Select a standard marine band VHF antenna compatible with VHF voice radios
Ensure antenna has sufficient cable length to reach the transceiver
Connect antenna to SO 239 connector on AIS transceiver using PL 259 connector
Verify cable impedance is 50 ohms
procedures.expected_outcome: VHF antenna properly connected to AIS transceiver

procedures.title: VHF Antenna Splitter Installation
steps: Obtain Navico NSPL-500 VHF Antenna Splitter
Connect existing antenna to splitter
Connect splitter to NAIS-500 transceiver
Connect splitter to VHF voice radio
procedures.expected_outcome: Single antenna working with both VHF radio and AIS transceiver

steps: Connect AIS transceiver to chartplotter using appropriate cables
Configure chartplotter to accept NMEA 0183 data at 38400 baud

Verify data transmission
procedures.expected_outcome: Chartplotter displaying AIS messages

steps: Connect AIS transceiver to NMEA 2000 network using supplied cable

Enable AIS target display in chart options

procedures.title: PC/Mac Connection
steps: Connect AIS transceiver to PC/Mac using USB connector
Install any required drivers
Configure charting software for AIS data input
Verify data reception
procedures.expected_outcome: PC/Mac displaying AIS messages

procedures.title: GPS Antenna Installation
preconditions: Clean mounting surface with no dirt, old paint, or debris
Have gasket and 2 small screws ready
steps: Mark and drill 2 mounting holes and additional hole for GPS cable if needed
Thread the attached cable through center of gasket
Install gasket
Screw GPS antenna to mounting surface
Route cable to AIS transceiver unit, adding extension cables if needed
Connect GPS antenna cable to GPS connector on AIS transceiver
procedures.expected_outcome: GPS antenna securely mounted and connected to AIS transceiver

procedures.title: VHF Antenna Connection
preconditions: Have standard marine band VHF antenna or AIS antenna
steps: Route cable from VHF antenna to AIS transceiver
Connect cable to VHF connector (SO239) on AIS transceiver
procedures.expected_outcome: VHF antenna properly connected to AIS transceiver

procedures.title: Connecting the Accessory Cable
preconditions: Have the supplied accessory cable ready
steps: Locate the connector marked 'PWR/0183' on the unit
Connect the pre-moulded connector end of the cable to the 'PWR/0183' port
Identify the eight color-coded bare wires on the other end
Connect red wire (Pin 8) to positive power supply (12-24V DC)
Connect black wire (Pin 9) to negative power supply
Connect light green wire (Pin 12) to external switch negative
Connect orange wire (Pin 10) to external switch positive for silent mode
Connect brown wire (Pin 1) to NMEA 0183 Port 1 TX+
Connect blue wire (Pin 2) to NMEA 0183 Port 1 TX-
Connect white wire (Pin 3) to NMEA 0183 Port 1 RX+
Connect green wire (Pin 4) to NMEA 0183 Port 1 RX-
Connect purple wire (Pin 11) to NMEA 0183 Port 2 TX+
Connect pink wire (Pin 7) to NMEA 0183 Port 2 TX-
Connect grey wire (Pin 6) to NMEA 0183 Port 2 RX+
Connect yellow wire (Pin 5) to NMEA 0183 Port 2 RX-
Double check all connections before applying power
procedures.expected_outcome: All wires properly connected according to color code and pin assignments
error_codes: Permanent damage may occur if wired incorrectly

procedures.title: Installing External Silent Mode Switch
preconditions: NAIS-500 AIS transceiver installation in progress
steps: Locate the light green and orange wires from the transceiver
Connect one terminal of toggle switch to light green wire
Connect other terminal of toggle switch to orange wire
procedures.expected_outcome: External switch installed for remote control of silent mode
error_codes: Do not connect voltage source across switch inputs - may cause damage

procedures.title: Connecting NMEA 0183 Port 1 (38,400 baud)
preconditions: NAIS-500 AIS transceiver installation in progress
steps: Connect brown wire (Transmit+) to equipment NMEA input+
Connect blue wire (Transmit-) to equipment NMEA input-
Connect white wire (Receive+) to equipment NMEA output+
Connect green wire (Receive-) to equipment NMEA output-
Configure connected equipment for 38,400 baud rate
procedures.expected_outcome: High-speed NMEA 0183 connection established

procedures.title: Connecting NMEA 0183 Port 2 (4,800 baud)
preconditions: NAIS-500 AIS transceiver installation in progress
steps: Connect purple wire (Transmit+) to equipment NMEA input+
Connect pink wire (Transmit-) to equipment NMEA input-
Connect grey wire (Receive+) to equipment NMEA output+
Connect yellow wire (Receive-) to equipment NMEA output-
Configure connected equipment for 4,800 baud rate
procedures.expected_outcome: Low-speed NMEA 0183 connection established

procedures.title: Power Connection
preconditions: NAIS-500 AIS transceiver installation in progress
steps: Connect red wire to power source positive (+)
Connect black wire to power source negative (-)
procedures.expected_outcome: Power properly connected to AIS transceiver
error_codes: Incorrect wiring may cause permanent damage

procedures.title: NMEA0183 Connection Wiring
steps: Connect Power in + wire (Red)
Connect Power in - wire (Black)
Connect Switch input + wire (Light green)
Connect Switch input - wire (Orange)
For Port 1: Connect Transmit + (Brown), Transmit - (Blue), Receive + (White), Receive - (Green)
For Port 2: Connect Transmit + (Purple), Transmit - (Pink), Receive + (Grey), Receive - (Yellow)
procedures.expected_outcome: NMEA0183 ports properly wired for data communication

procedures.title: NMEA 2000 Network Connection
steps: Connect AIS transceiver to NMEA 2000 network using Navico cable
Ensure chartplotter is connected to same NMEA 2000 network
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS targets visible on chartplotter

procedures.title: USB Connection Setup
preconditions: PC or Mac with USB port
steps: Connect USB cable between AIS transceiver and computer
Wait for automatic device detection
Select new COM port in navigation software
Set baud rate to 38,400
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS data accessible through PC/Mac

procedures.title: USB Connection Reset Procedure
steps: Disconnect power from AIS unit
Close all PC/Mac applications using USB connection
Reapply power to AIS unit
Relaunch applications
Reconnect USB cable
procedures.expected_outcome: USB connection restored

procedures.title: Power Supply Connection
steps: Connect red wire to power supply positive terminal
Connect black wire to power supply negative terminal
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver powered on

procedures.title: Initial Power-Up Check
steps: Apply power to the AIS transceiver
Observe LED indicator pattern
Verify PWR (Green) indicates unit is powered and operating normally
Check ERR (Red) for any errors or invalid MMSI
Observe Rx (Green) flashing when receiving AIS data
Check Tx (Orange) for silent mode status
procedures.expected_outcome: Unit powers up and LED indicators show proper operational status
error_codes: Red ERR LED: Error or invalid MMSI

procedures.title: NAIS System Configurator Installation - PC
steps: Insert CD into PC
Navigate to NAIS System Configurator folder
Open Windows folder
Run setup.exe file
Follow on-screen prompts
If security warning appears, click Run
Wait for installation to complete
procedures.expected_outcome: NAIS System Configurator launches automatically with start menu folder and shortcut created

procedures.title: NAIS System Configurator Installation - Mac
steps: Insert CD into Mac
Navigate to NAIS System Configurator folder
Open OSX folder
Double click NAIS System Configurator.dmg file
Follow on-screen instructions
procedures.expected_outcome: NAIS System Configurator successfully installed on Mac

procedures.title: Wire Connection Procedure
steps: Connect Power in + to Red wire
Connect Power in – to Black wire
Connect Switch input + to Light green wire
Connect Switch input – to Orange wire
Connect NMEA0183 Transmit + to Brown wire
Connect Port 1 Transmit – to Blue wire
Connect 38,400 baud Receive + to White wire
Connect chart plotter Receive – to Green wire
Connect NMEA0183 Transmit + to Purple wire
Connect Port 2 Transmit – to Pink wire
Connect 4,800 baud Receive + to Grey wire
Connect other NMEA0183 device Receive – to Yellow wire
procedures.expected_outcome: All wires properly connected according to color code specification

procedures.title: Initial Software Installation
steps: Double click the NAIS System Configurator.dmg file
Follow on-screen instructions to complete installation
procedures.expected_outcome: NAIS System Configurator software installed successfully

procedures.title: AIS Transceiver Configuration
preconditions: Required vessel information available (MMSI, vessel name, type, call sign, dimensions, GPS antenna position)
steps: Connect AIS transceiver via USB (for configuration only)
Launch NAIS System Configurator
Enter MMSI number (can only be done once)
Enter vessel name
Enter vessel type
Enter call sign
Enter vessel dimensions
Enter GPS antenna installation position
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver configured with vessel information

procedures.title: Silent Mode Operation
preconditions: External switch connected to AIS transceiver
steps: Activate external switch to enter silent mode
Verify orange light on Tx indicator is illuminated
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver enters silent mode - stops transmitting position while continuing to receive

procedures.title: Normal Operation Mode
steps: Power on unit
Wait up to six minutes for full vessel details to become visible to others
Monitor chartplotter or PC for AIS data from other vessels
procedures.expected_outcome: AIS transceiver transmitting and receiving vessel information

procedures.title: Interpreting PWR Indicator Status
preconditions: AIS transceiver is connected to power
steps: Observe PWR indicator light
If green steady light is shown, unit is powered up correctly
procedures.expected_outcome: Confirmation of proper power status

procedures.title: Checking MMSI Programming Status
steps: Observe ERR indicator light
If red steady light is shown, MMSI needs programming
If red flashing light is shown, system error detected or unit is connected to USB for initial programming
procedures.expected_outcome: Determination of MMSI programming status

procedures.title: Monitoring AIS Reception
steps: Observe Rx indicator light
Green flashing light indicates active AIS data reception
procedures.expected_outcome: Confirmation of AIS data reception

procedures.title: Monitoring AIS Transmission Status
steps: Observe Tx indicator light
Orange flashing: Unit is acquiring GPS fix (no transmission)
Orange steady: Unit is in silent mode (no transmission)
Green flashing: Unit is transmitting AIS data
For green flashing - note flash interval:
- 3 minute intervals when vessel speed under 2 knots
- 30 second intervals when vessel speed above 2 knots
procedures.expected_outcome: Understanding of current transmission status

procedures.title: GPS Fix Acquisition Monitoring
steps: Observe Tx indicator for orange flashing light
If newly powered on: Wait several minutes for GPS fix
If GPS fix is lost: Unit will attempt reacquisition for 30 minutes
If no fix after 30 minutes: Unit will enter BIIT system error state
procedures.expected_outcome: Successful GPS position fix acquisition

procedures.title: No Data Reception Troubleshooting
preconditions: Chartplotter not receiving data from AIS
steps: Check power supply connection
Verify power supply is 12V or 24V
Verify chartplotter connections are correct
procedures.expected_outcome: Chartplotter receiving data from AIS

procedures.title: No Indicators Illuminated Troubleshooting
preconditions: No indicator lights visible on unit
steps: Check power supply connection
Verify power supply is 12V or 24V
procedures.expected_outcome: Indicator lights functioning properly

procedures.title: Red Error Indicator Troubleshooting
steps: Check MMSI configuration and validity
Inspect VHF antenna connection and condition
Verify GPS antenna connection and installation
Review GPS signal strength graph in NAIS System Configurator
Verify power supply is within 9.6V to 31.2V range
Contact dealer if issue persists
procedures.expected_outcome: Red error indicator turns off

procedures.title: Vessel Name Not Displaying Troubleshooting
preconditions: MMSI visible but vessel name not showing on other devices
steps: Verify other vessel's AIS device supports message 24
Recommend software upgrade for receiving vessel's equipment
Confirm other vessel updates AIS unit and/or chart-plotting software
procedures.expected_outcome: Vessel name visible on other devices

procedures.title: NAIS-500 Technical Specifications Reference
steps: Verify power requirements: DC 9.6V - 31.2V
Check average power consumption: 180mA at 12 VDC
Confirm peak current rating: 2A at 12 VDC
Verify physical dimensions: 152 x 98 x 52 mm (L x W x H)
Confirm unit weight: 260g
Ensure GPS receiver is 50 channel IEC 61108-1 compliant
Verify NMEA 0183 baud rates: 38,400 and 4,800
Confirm NMEA 2000 LEN=1 compatibility
Check VHF frequency range: 156.025 to 162.025 MHz in 25 kHz steps
Verify output power: 33 dBm ± 1.5 dB
procedures.expected_outcome: All specifications match required parameters for proper operation

procedures.title: NAIS-500 Connection Verification
steps: Check VHF antenna connector (SΟ-239)
Verify external GPS antenna connector (SMA)
Confirm USB type mini-B connection
Check NMEA 2000 standard connector
Verify 12-way power input/NMEA 0183/external switch connection
procedures.expected_outcome: All connections are properly seated and functional

procedures.title: Operating Environment Requirements
preconditions: Device must be installed in protected location
steps: Ensure operating temperature remains between -15ºC to +55ºC
Maintain water resistant rating of IP67
Follow IEC 60945 'Protected' category guidelines
procedures.expected_outcome: Device operates within safe environmental parameters

procedures.title: Status Indicator Monitoring
steps: Check Power indicator status
Monitor Error indicator
Verify Rx indicator operation
Observe Tx indicator for silent mode status
procedures.expected_outcome: All status indicators showing correct operation

procedures.title: VHF Transceiver Operation
steps: Verify frequency range of 156.025 to 162.025 MHz
Confirm channel bandwidth of 25 kHz
Monitor output power maintains 33 dBm ± 1.5 dB
Ensure proper GMSK modulation for AIS
Verify AFSK modulation for DSC reception
procedures.expected_outcome: Transceiver operating within specified parameters
